text:
anya: quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak yesterday i'm seeing a 7-12% p99 increase for multi-variant routes (especially when compat sets mix quantized and fp16 variants).
kevin: ugh. which routes / models? any KV cache stats?
mohit: sounds like batch formation is changing. mixing variants often forces smaller batches due to compat checks. did we change the kernel fallback order?
anya: route: /v1/generate (multi-variant: redwood-ggml-q4_1 + rw-ggml-fp16). KV hit-rate dropped ~4pp on those hosts during the window. logs show more fragmenting: many single-request batches.
sara: @anya can you paste the profiling snippet? especially scheduler/batcher metrics.
anya: sure — from the node where it's bad:```
BATCHER: 2026-03-15 09:14:12 batch_formation_time_ms=12 queues=[q0:8 q1:1 q2:0] avg_batch_size=1.9 token_budget_target=2048 compat_rejects=34
KVCACHE: hits=941 misses=63 cold_warmups=12 hit_rate=0.937
KERNEL_SELECT: preferred=fp16 fallback=>q4_1 (fallbacks=28)
```
mohit: batch_formation_time went up and avg_batch_size down. token_budget_target 2048 may be too aggressive with mixed variants — we fall back to slower kernel which reduces throughput and increases queue drain time -> fragmenting.
kevin: hypothesis: kernel-selection reorder added a stricter compatibility check causing early fallback to fp16 kernels that don't accept q4 cached KV layout. That forces KV cold-warmups and breaks prefix caching.
anya: agree. i also noticed the routing policy now does per-request variant pinning for safety; it reduces opportunities to coalesce compatible requests.
sara: can we try two quick experiments: 1) relax token_budget target so batches wait longer (bump to 3072) 2) prefer kernel that accepts q4 cache layout even if slightly slower single-token, to preserve batchability and KV hits.
mohit: +1. also tweak compat set grouping: put q4 and fp16 into same compat set for routing so we don't route to different variants unless necessary. this would increase fanout risk though.
kevin: tradeoff: grouping increases batching but may increase quantization mismatch regressions. need eval harness for quality. can we run short A/B with canary routing?
anya: i ran a quick canary on one pool with token_budget=3072 and compat_grouping enabled. results: p95 down 3%, p99 down 8%, KV hit_rate up 2.6pp. latency tail improved. quality delta within noise for our eval set.
per-fact: perf-bot: perf-regression-check completed for canary pool (id: pool-17). metrics: p99 -7.9%, cost_tokens -1.2%, kl-divergence vs baseline 0.0009 (within threshold). :white_check_mark:
mohit: nice. let's codify changes: revert the kernel-selection reordering that enforces strict layout mismatch, add a fallback preference table that biases toward cache-compatible kernels, and increase token_budget target for multi-variant routes by default.
sara: can we implement a queue policy toggle? i.e. for multi-variant endpoints set queue.wait_ms = 20 (instead of 5) and token_budget=3072; keep single-variant endpoints as-is.
kevin: sounds good. we should also add a profiler counter to track "compat-induced fragmentation" (count of requests dropped from batch due to compat mismatch) so we can alert earlier.
anya: i'll open a PR with the preference table change + compat meter. i'll also attach the canary config and results.
anya: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/serve/+/2345 — includes config snippet:```
routing:
  multi_variant_defaults:
    token_budget: 3072
    queue_wait_ms: 20
    compat_groups:
      - [rw-ggml-q4_1, rw-ggml-q4_0]
      - [rw-ggml-fp16]
kernel_selection:
  prefer_cache_compatible: true
  fallback_order:
    - cache_compatible
    - performance_first
```
sara: canary looks safe. ops: can we roll to dedicated pools tomorrow morning low-traffic window? @deploy-bot please schedule.
deploy-bot: scheduled rollout to pool-17 at 2026-03-16T03:00:00Z window=2h owner=sara
kevin: follow-ups: (1) add compat-induced-fragmentation metric to console dashboards, (2) run regen eval for potential small quality drift on mixed workloads, (3) run a larger canary across 5 pools.
mohit: i'll handle dashboard and instrument counters. anya — ping me when PR is merged, i'll coordinate canary expansion.
anya: will do. thanks all. moving action items into the ticket. :thumbsup:
